provenance.decision: OWNER 2026-08-11: 'colour theme and branding must freez as we have in website'. The WEBSITE is canonical and FROZEN for brand colour. The platform moves to it. Where the two disagree, the website's value wins.
provenance.dark: crowagent-website/astro/src/styles/tokens.css - the V6 hue shelf and ground ladder, which is what crowagent.ai actually serves.
provenance.light: crowagent-website/concepts/platform-theme/theme.css [data-mode='light'] - the website-authored, contrast-measured light column for the platform (contrast.mjs / ratios.json in that directory, zero failures).
provenance.note: The astro dark ladder is one revision NEWER than the concept's dark column (floor 02040A vs 03040A, canvas 050814 vs 05070E, panel 0B1024 vs 0C1020). The shipping astro values win. Every one of the three is DARKER than the concept's, so every contrast ratio the concept measured against light ink improves rather than regresses.

voidedAudit.what: The platform UI/UX audit brief section 3 names rgb(4,14,26) (#040E1A) as the foundation to preserve.
voidedAudit.status: VOID ON COLOUR - owner 2026-08-11. That audit ran against the platform's CURRENT theme with a tool that had no knowledge of the brand change, so it DESCRIBES the defect rather than stating the target. #040E1A is not a preserve-target.

light.why: NOT the website's derived light teal #0F766E. Platform --teal in light is a FILL that carries --on-accent (#04121E) as its label: #04121E on #0F766E measures 3.43:1 and fails WCAG AA, where #04121E on #0A9A80 measures 5.4:1. #0F766E is teal-as-INK and only becomes correct once the V6 control-neutrality work lands (ADOPTION.md A4/A5), which is a separate programme. Light is NOT flattened onto the dark value.

brand-teal-deep.role: the teal hover / pressed step. Platform --teal-d.

light.why: measured 5.22:1 against --bg (DYN-A11Y-03). Follows brand-teal, which is platform-held in light for the reason above.

ground-3.role: elevated / inset wells and tracks. Platform --surf2.

ground-4.role: deepest inset / pressed / row-hover. Platform --surf3 AND --surf4, which collapse.

ink-2.role: muted secondary / tertiary text. Platform --mist AND --dim-c, which collapse.

accent-nest.role: the blue product accent. Platform --nest. Painted as TEXT by .product-name-nest (web/app/globals-brand.css:192) and by the portal log feed's INFO level (apps/portal/src/components/ui/LogFeed.tsx:5), and as the StatusPill blue status DOT (packages/ui/src/primitives/status-pill.tsx:30).

light.why: [R281-TOKENS-NEST-SIGHT-LIGHT-DECISION-01 2026-09-03] The light column gave --nest no override at all, so it inherited the dark neon onto the near-white canvas at 2.11 to 2.54:1 across the four light grounds, failing the 4.5:1 AA text floor and the 3:1 WCAG 1.4.11 non-text floor at once. Exactly the defect class tokens.css records as X-2 (--coral), X-3 (--gold and --lime) and X-5 (--crowmark). THE METHOD IS THE ONE THOSE FOUR USED, and no hex is invented here. X-3 states it: keep the hue and drop the lightness until every real call site clears AA. X-2 and X-5 add the part that matters more, which is that the deepened value is RECOVERED from somewhere the estate already holds it rather than minted. It is held here too. The portal shipped its own light --nest on 2026-08-09 with a comment saying canonical light is missing them and asking for platform follow up, so this is that follow up and the value is the portal's own, unchanged. Hue 213 degrees goes to 203, the same order of hue drift as --gold (43 to 42), --mark (258 to 262) and --crowmark (258 to 262). MEASURED with the WCAG 2.1 relative luminance formula, L(#60A5FA)=0.362992 and L(#19618E)=0.107091, on the four grounds of the frozen light column. AS TEXT: --surf #FFFFFF 2.54 to 6.68, --bg #F5F6FA 2.35 to 6.19, --surf2 #EDF0F7 2.23 to 5.86, --bg-deep/--surf3/--surf4 #E7EAF2 2.11 to 5.55. All four FAIL to PASS at 4.5:1. AS A STATUS DOT the ground is the Badge info wash, --blue-d rgba(11,105,163,0.12) composited over each ground, not the bare ground: 2.14 to 5.62 on #E2EDF4, 1.99 to 5.23 on #D9E5F0, 1.89 to 4.97 on #D2E0ED, 1.80 to 4.74 on #CDDBE9. All four FAIL to PASS at 3:1. DARK IS UNTOUCHED and stays 8.06 / 7.86 / 7.42 / 7.29 / 6.54:1 as text across the five dark grounds and 6.81 / 6.56 / 5.99 / 5.83 / 5.14:1 as a dot on the dark info wash. NO COMPANION RULE IS NEEDED, and that was checked rather than assumed, because the inversion hazard X-2, X-3 and TD-26 all warn about only bites a token used as a solid FILL under a near-black label. Every consumer was enumerated: two text uses, two dot uses, and the Tailwind alias --color-prod-nest in web/app/globals.css:179 which resolves through the cascade. There is no --nest fill carrying text.

accent-sight.role: the pink product accent. Platform --sight. Painted as TEXT by .product-name-sight (web/app/globals-brand.css:189) and as the StatusPill pink status DOT (packages/ui/src/primitives/status-pill.tsx:33, and the portal agent dot at apps/portal/src/app/portal/agents/[slug]/page.tsx:90).

light.why: [R281-TOKENS-NEST-SIGHT-LIGHT-DECISION-01 2026-09-03] Same defect and same derivation as accent-nest above. Before, the dark neon measured 2.20 to 2.65:1 on the four light grounds, under both floors. The value is the portal's own light --sight, already shipping, so nothing that renders today changes. TWO INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS LANDED ON THE SAME HEX, which is why it is recorded as the value rather than merely accepted: stepping the pink ramp down from the 400 rung this pigment sits on, the way --mark went violet 400 to 600 and --coral went red 400 to 700, the first rung that clears 4.5:1 on ALL FOUR frozen light grounds is the 700 rung #BE185D. The 600 rung #DB2777 reaches only 3.82:1 on #E7EAF2 and fails, which is why the step is 400 to 700 here and not 400 to 600. Hue 329 degrees goes to 335. MEASURED with the WCAG 2.1 relative luminance formula, L(#F472B6)=0.346451 and L(#BE185D)=0.123907. AS TEXT: --surf 2.65 to 6.04, --bg 2.45 to 5.59, --surf2 2.32 to 5.29, --bg-deep/--surf3/--surf4 2.20 to 5.02. All four FAIL to PASS at 4.5:1. AS A STATUS DOT the ground is the Badge product wash, --teal-dim rgba(10,154,128,0.10) composited over each ground: 2.36 to 5.39 on #E7F5F2, 2.20 to 5.02 on #DEEDEE, 2.08 to 4.74 on #D6E7EB, 1.99 to 4.53 on #D1E2E7. All four FAIL to PASS at 3:1. DARK IS UNTOUCHED at 7.74 / 7.54 / 7.12 / 7.00 / 6.28:1 as text and 6.81 / 6.58 / 6.00 / 5.90 / 5.17:1 as a dot. NO COMPANION RULE IS NEEDED for the same enumerated reason as accent-nest: --sight paints text and dots only, never a fill under a label.

ladderNotes.surfaces: Six platform ground steps map onto five website ones; --surf3 and --surf4 collapse onto ground-4. That collapse is the website's own finding, not a choice made here (concepts/platform-theme/README.md section 3, 'Six platform steps to five website ones; --surf3 and --surf4 collapse'). Assignment is by LIGHTNESS ORDER within each mode, which is why the website token a slot draws from differs between modes: the light ladder is not a mirror of the dark one (light --c-raised is already #FFFFFF, so light lights DOWNWARD as a surface recedes). Monotonicity is preserved in both modes, so no existing elevation relationship inverts.
ladderNotes.surfacesLightExtraCollapse: The light column offers only FOUR distinct grounds (#FFFFFF, #F5F6FA, #EDF0F7, #E7EAF2), so in light --bg-deep, --surf3 and --surf4 all land on ground-4/#E7EAF2. Three tokens on one value. This is a property of the source, not an invention.
ladderNotes.ink: Four platform ink steps map onto three website ones; --mist and --dim-c collapse onto ink-2. The website's own mapping table names --steel/--mist as the merging pair on nearest-VALUE grounds; this file merges --mist/--dim-c instead, on ROLE grounds, because the platform documents --steel and --mist as deliberately non-interchangeable (R24-UIDE-004) and --dim-c is the tertiary step that has no website counterpart. Dark --dim-c #7E96B0 -> #A9B6D2 and light #6B7688 -> #5A6478 both INCREASE contrast against their own ground.

unreconciled.reason: RULE 0-C: never invent, guess or estimate a brand value. The website palette contains no counterpart for these, so they are NAMED here rather than derived.

tokens.--teal-l: #6EE9D2 - lighter teal step. No website counterpart.
tokens.--line-deep: #1E3A58 - navy rule. No website counterpart; still on the OLD navy family.
tokens.--bg-tint: #04101A - tinted page wash. No website counterpart; still on the OLD navy family.
tokens.--sky/--gold/--core/--trace: the website palette has two hues and two markers and no home for these accents (concepts/platform-theme/README.md section 3). [R281-TOKENS-NEST-SIGHT-LIGHT-DECISION-01 2026-09-03] --nest and --sight LEFT this list. They are pigments now, accent-nest and accent-sight above. Being unreconciled was harmless for a token that has a value in every theme, and it was NOT harmless for these two: an unreconciled accent with no light value at all inherits its dark neon onto the near-white canvas, which is how both sat at 2.11 to 2.65:1 while every drift guard stayed green. Their light values are platform-held, recovered from the portal rather than derived from the website palette, so the website still has no counterpart and the record still invents nothing. The remaining four are text-safe or unmeasured on this pass and stay here.
tokens.--ca-mark-text: [R27-A11Y-CONTRAST-01 2026-08-16] #A78BFA dark / #6D28D9 light - the --mark family used AS TEXT, which is the violet counterpart of --ca-teal-text and the thing --on-mark is NOT (--on-mark is text ON a --mark fill; this is --mark's own family acting as ink). UNBOUND ON PURPOSE, and named here so it is not merely invisible: this file carries NO violet pigment at all, and --mark is in neverTouch above because it is already byte-identical to the website's --c-violet. There is therefore nothing to bind it TO, and minting a violet pigment to create one would be inventing a brand value, which RULE 0-C forbids. NEITHER VALUE IS NEW: the dark half is the dark --mark itself (so dark theme is byte-unchanged), and the light half is the hex --crowmark-text and the light --crowmark already hold. WHY IT EXISTS: .st-mark in web/app/styles/layout.css painted var(--mark) as 11px/700 TEXT on an 18% wash of itself and axe measured 4.04:1 against the 4.5:1 AA floor on every contract sub-route; --crowmark-text could not be reused directly because it is theme-INVARIANT #6D28D9 and would have measured 2.20:1 on the dark wash, breaking a passing surface. MEASURED with the WCAG 2.1 formula: light 4.05 -> 5.04 on the --bg wash, clearing 4.5:1 on all five light grounds (worst 4.57 on --surf3/--bg-deep); dark unchanged at 5.75 on --bg, with --surf3 a recorded 4.4973/4.5197 BOUNDARY that predates this token and is not fixable without a lighter violet the palette does not have.
tokens.--err/--warn/--success/--coral: the website palette carries no red and no green. The concept derives --p-danger #FF7A85 dark / #B32131 light but binding it is the role-layer programme, not a value swap.
tokens.light --scrim-modal: declared as rgba(10, 31, 58, a) in the light block, channels taken from the OLD dark --surf. Left as found; no website counterpart for a light scrim. [R27-DS-BORDER-01 2026-08-18] `light --border` USED TO SHARE THIS ENTRY and is no longer unreconciled: the whole light structural ramp was rgba(17,28,45,a), a channel triple that is in no pigment in this record and therefore had no source at all, while every drift guard stayed green because an unbound key is invisible to them. It is bound to ink-1 now at luminance-matched alphas. The scrim is a different shape of problem and stays here: it is a full-viewport wash, not a hairline, so there is nothing to luminance-match it against.
tokens.light --ca-teal-text: #0A6E5C - the light-canvas teal INK / rescue FILL. Platform-held, no website counterpart, so only its DARK value is bound (to brand-teal, blocks root+dark). It is a THIRD light teal on purpose and not redundancy: --teal #0A9A80 is the resting fill (5.36:1 under an obsidian label), --teal-d #077663 is the hover/pressed STEP, and this is the value the DYN-A11Y-01/02/04/05 rescue rules pin when a teal fill has to carry a WHITE label or teal has to act as ink. Collapsing it onto --teal-d would clear every floor (5.55:1 both ways vs 6.18/5.97) but would make a rescued control stop changing colour on hover - the same defect the Word task pane shipped. MEASURED 2026-08-11 against the frozen light grounds: as ink 5.97:1 on #FFFFFF, 5.14:1 on the deepest ground #E7EAF2, 5.45:1 on the --teal-dim wash; as fill under white 6.18:1. [CLOSED 2026-08-11] Seven consuming declarations in web/app/globals.css and apps/portal/src/app/globals.css re-typed this hex instead of reading the token that already held it; they now read var(--ca-teal-text).
tokens.light --ca-fg-muted (CLOSED 2026-08-11): WAS UNBOUND IN LIGHT and had duly drifted. It was declared `#586577` with the comment '= light --mist', but the freeze moved light --mist to #5A6478, so the alias and the token it claims to mirror held DIFFERENT values while every drift guard stayed green; an unbound key is invisible to the guard, which is the same shape as the LIGHT_THEME_TOKENS finding recorded in platformConstantBindings._lightGroupNote. It is a branding defect rather than a contrast one: #586577 measured 5.20:1 on light --surf2 against #5A6478's 5.22:1, so nothing was failing. Bound to ink-2 in all three blocks now, which is what --mist, --dim-c and --ca-fg-disabled already were.
tokens.--teal-40 / --teal-45 in the dark block: MEASURED ABSENT: unlike their eleven --teal-NN siblings these two are declared only at :root and are NOT re-asserted in [data-theme="dark"]. Bound at root only, because this generator never inserts a declaration. Harmless today (:root IS the dark palette) but it is the same shape as the light-OS freeze defect the tokens suite guards elsewhere, and it is recorded here rather than silently patched.

neverTouch.--mark: #A78BFA CrowMark product identity. Already byte-identical to the website's --c-violet.

platformBindings._templateSyntax: {hex:PIGMENT} -> #RRGGBB ; {rgb:PIGMENT} -> 'r, g, b'. A binding is applied ONLY to blocks listed in `blocks` AND only where the declaration already exists - the generator never inserts a token.
platformBindings._rootUses: The :root block holds the DARK palette (color-scheme: dark). Bindings listing 'root' therefore resolve against the pigment's DARK value; 'light'/'dark' resolve against their own.
platformBindings._accentNote: [R281-TOKENS-NEST-SIGHT-LIGHT-DECISION-01 2026-09-03] The two product accents that had a light value nowhere. They are bound in ALL THREE blocks on purpose. root and dark carry the same dark hex, and the dark block is not redundant: tokens.css records the light-OS freeze mechanism at length, where a var() in a custom-property value is substituted on the declaring <html>, so any token that gains a light override MUST also restate its dark value in [data-theme="dark"] or a dark-pinned subtree rendered for a light-OS visitor inherits the deep light value onto dark navy. packages/tokens/src/__tests__/tokens.test.ts enforces that for the whole class. The generator never inserts a declaration, so all six declarations were added to tokens.css by hand first and the VALUES come from here.
platformBindings._borderRampNote: [R27-DS-BORDER-01 2026-08-18] THE NEUTRAL STRUCTURAL RAMP. Spec 6.2 records the defect: the @crowagent/ui Card `default` variant drew its STRUCTURAL edge with --border2, brand teal at 20% alpha, so structure spoke the language of state. R27-CROWMARK-A had already fixed exactly this in the LIGHT block by moving --border/--border2/--border3 to a neutral navy; the DARK block was left on teal, so one ramp still split by theme. THE DERIVATION, and no value is authored here: a structural border is pigment `ink-1` laid over the ground, at the alpha that makes its composite relative luminance on ground-2 (the card ground, --surf) EQUAL to the outgoing value's. Visual weight is therefore preserved by construction and only HUE changes, which is precisely the defect and precisely the extent of the fix. ink-1 is the pigment this record ALREADY draws every non-brand structural line from (--chart-grid, --chart-grid-strong and BORDER_TOKENS.borderSub are all ink-1 at alpha), so the ramp introduces no new pigment and mints no new hex. SOLVED ALPHAS (WCAG 2.1 relative luminance, sRGB alpha composite, bisection to 1e-9). Dark, from the teal ramp: --border .10 gives 0.0832 rounded 0.08; --border2 .20 gives 0.1683 rounded 0.17; --border3 .32 gives 0.2712 rounded 0.27; --border-strong .62 gives 0.5296 rounded 0.53. Light, from the rgba(17,28,45,a) literals the light block held UNBOUND: --border .10 gives 0.1112 rounded 0.11; --border2 .32 gives 0.3559 rounded 0.36; --border3 .45 gives 0.5004 rounded 0.50; --border-subtle .07 gives 0.0778 rounded 0.08; --border-strong .55 gives 0.6117 rounded 0.61. --border-strong is the ONE rung carrying a contrast requirement (WCAG 1.4.11, 3:1 for the boundary of a UI component) so it was RE-MEASURED rather than assumed safe on the strength of the luminance match. Dark, across --bg-deep/--bg/--surf/--surf2/--surf3-4: 4.50/4.51/4.50/4.49/4.33:1 after, against 4.57/4.56/4.49/4.47/4.23:1 before. Light: 3.58/3.73/3.85/3.65/3.58:1 after, against 3.66/3.78/3.86/3.72/3.66:1 before. Every ground clears 3:1 in both themes and the dark WORST ground improves, so no boundary is weakened. The bare minimum alpha for 3:1 is 0.4033 dark and 0.5401 light, so 0.53 and 0.61 keep the headroom policy X-6 set. TEAL IS NOT BANNED, IT IS CONFINED TO STATE: --glass-border and --glass-border-hover are de-aliased below to explicit teal literals byte-identical to what they resolve to today, so the decorative glass edge keeps the hue it was drawn with rather than being neutralised as collateral, and .ca-settings-card[data-tone='accent'] already spells --teal-20 for the selected step.

platformConstantBindings._why: constants.ts is a TypeScript MIRROR of the same palette, for consumers that cannot read a CSS custom property: Chart.js (canvas), the email templates, the PDF/DOCX/OG generators. A hand-maintained mirror is the same RULE 0-C defect as an independent website palette, one file closer in. MEASURED, 2026-08-11, before this pass touched anything: BRAND_COLOR_TOKENS.teal and CA_ALIAS_TOKENS.teal held #33D9BD while tokens.css held #0CC9A8, and TEXT_SCALE_TOKENS.dimC held #7A9AAE while tokens.css held #7E96B0. The mirror had ALREADY drifted from the file it mirrors, in three places, with nothing failing. It is generated from here now.
platformConstantBindings._note: These consumers are dark-only today (CHART_COLOURS carries a header saying so). Every binding resolves against the pigment's DARK value.
platformConstantBindings._borderMirrorNote: [R27-DS-BORDER-01 2026-08-18] These three follow the CSS ramp onto ink-1 at the solved alphas; see platformBindings._borderRampNote for the derivation. They are rebound rather than left alone because an unbound or stale mirror key is exactly the silent drift this file exists to stop, and borderSub was ALREADY ink-1 at 0.12, which is the precedent the whole ramp is derived from. NOT ADDED, DELIBERATELY: no borderSubtle / borderDefault / borderStrong keys are minted here. The generator never inserts, BorderTokens is a typed interface, and the consumers of this mirror are Chart.js, the email templates and the PDF/DOCX/OG generators, none of which draws a settings card. Adding three keys nothing reads would be surface for its own sake; they are named here so the absence is a decision rather than an oversight.
platformConstantBindings._productAccentMirrorNote: [R281-TOKENS-NEST-SIGHT-LIGHT-DECISION-01 2026-09-03] nest and sight are bound here at their DARK values, which they already held, so this changes no byte. It is not a no-op: an unbound mirror key is invisible to the drift guard, which is the failure this whole file exists to stop, and these two keys now hold a value that has a recorded source. NOT ADDED, DELIBERATELY: no nest or sight key is minted in LIGHT_THEME_TOKENS. That group is the print canvas the PDF, DOCX and XLSX generators paint on. It draws no status dot and no product name, the generator never inserts a key, and adding two nothing reads would be surface for its own sake. The light values live in tokens.css where the two real consumers read them.
platformConstantBindings._lightGroupNote: LIGHT_THEME_TOKENS is the PRINT / light canvas the PDF, DOCX and XLSX generators paint on, and it is the ONE colour group in constants.ts that is not dark. Bound with the @light mode suffix. MEASURED 2026-08-11, before these bindings existed: ten of its twelve colour keys disagreed with the reconciled [data-theme="light"] block in tokens.css that they cite in their own comments (bg #F6F8FB vs #F5F6FA, bgDeep #EEF2F7 vs #E7EAF2, surf2 #F2F5F9 vs #EDF0F7, surf3 #E9EEF5 vs #E7EAF2, surf4 #DFE6F0 vs #E7EAF2, cloud #14181F vs #0B0E19, steel #3A4655 vs #2B3245, mist #586577 vs #5A6478, dimC #6B7688 vs #5A6478). Only teal/tealD already agreed. An UNBOUND key is invisible to the drift guard, so this group drifted silently while every bound key was green. gridPrint, inkPrint, ragRed, ragGreen, ragRedTint, ragAmberTint and coralPrint are deliberately NOT bound: brand.source.json records no counterpart for them, they ship on customer documents today, and inventing one would breach RULE 0-C. They are named here so their absence is a recorded decision rather than an oversight.
